Shri Shrikrishna Sharma - Advocate for respondent No.1

Order 
Per: Justice Pradeep Mittal

The petitioner has filed the present Misc. Petition challenging the order dated 01.05.2025 passed by Central Administrative Tribunal Bench at Jabalpur in Original Application No.200/70/2023 whereby employment assistance in lieu of their acquired land has been denied.
2. The petitioner had earlier filed an Original Application before the learned Central Administrative Tribunal, Jabalpur Bench, challenging the impugned orders dated 13.02.2018 and 22.07.2020 passed by the respondent authorities.

entities.text: Central Administrative Tribunal Bench at Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the said Original Application, the petitioner prayed for a direction to the respondents to consider his claim for appointment in the Indian Railways on account of acquisition of his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 2 MP-3916-2025 parental land for a railway project.

It was contended that under the policy/scheme of the Railways,
employment assistance is provided to land losers whose lands have been acquired for railway projects, and several similarly situated persons have already been granted appointment under the said scheme.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that the learned Tribunal has dismissed the Original Application on an erroneous presumption by comparing the petitioner's case with O.A. No. 284/2025, which,
according to the petitioner, bears no similarity to the present matter.

According to petitioner, he is Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97004155/
1 claiming appointment in the Indian Railways under the scheme providing employment assistance to persons whose lands have been acquired for railway projects, and several similarly situated land losers have already been granted appointments under the said policy.
4. Learned counsel further submits that the solitary ground on which the petitioner's claim has been rejected by the respondents is that at the time of submission of his initial application he had not passed the 10th standard examination.

entities.text: Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the respondents have completely ignored the subsequent factual development that the petitioner has now passed the said examination and thereafter submitted a fresh application seeking appointment in lieu of acquisition of his land.

It is argued that the applicable policy of the Indian Railways clearly provides that in cases where land has been acquired prior to 11.11.2019, the benefit of appointment cannot be denied merely on the ground that the application NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 3 MP-3916-2025 was submitted after the said date.
5. Learned counsel submits that the petitioner's land had admittedly been acquired prior to the said cut-off date and therefore his case was required to be considered under the prevailing policy.

It is further contended that even in similar matters the learned Tribunal has granted relief, including in O.A. No. 745/2021 (Charan Prakash Kushwaha vs. Union of India) decided on 09.05.2022, and the Indian Railways itself has issued a clarification dated 05.03.2021 stating that if the land had been acquired prior to 11.11.2019, applications received even after the said date are required to be considered in accordance with the applicable rules.

entities.text: O.A. No. 745/2021 (Charan Prakash Kushwaha vs. Union of India)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that the said clarification has been completely ignored by the respondents as well as by the learned Tribunal.

It is also submitted that the action of the respondents is discriminatory inasmuch as in several similar cases the respondents have relaxed the educational qualification and granted appointment subject to the condition that the candidate would acquire the requisite qualification within a stipulated period, as was done in the case of one Sanjay Kumar, who was granted appointment subject to acquiring the requisite qualification within five years from the date of appointment i.e., 22.02.2016.

However, the petitioner's claim has been rejected by orders dated 13.02.2018 and 22.07.2020,
which amounts to hostile discrimination.

It is therefore submitted that the action of the respondents is arbitrary and violative of the guarantees enshrined under Articles 14, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 4 MP-3916-2025 16 and 21 of the Constitution of India, and that the learned Tribunal has committed a grave error in dismissing the Original Application of the petitioner.

Accordingly, learned counsel prays that the impugned order dated 01.05.2025 passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal, Jabalpur Bench, deserves to be set aside and the respondents be directed to consider and grant appointments to the petitioner under the applicable scheme for land losers.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and have carefully perused the material available on record.
6. From the record it is evident that the petitioner had applied pursuant to the notification dated 14.10.2016 issued by the West Central Railway for appointment on the basis of land acquisition.

As per the said notification, the minimum educational qualification prescribed for appointment in Group 'D' category was 10th pass or ITI or equivalent, as also reflected in the circulars issued by the Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97004155/
2 Railway Board dated 05.01.2011 and 09.12.2013.

entities.text: Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in the application submitted by the petitioner, his educational qualification was mentioned as Class VIII passed.
Thus, on the date of submission of the application the petitioner admittedly did not possess the minimum educational qualification required under the applicable policy.

7. It is further apparent from the record that the petitioner obtained the 10th standard qualification only on 07.09.2021, which was much after the issuance of the Railway Board Circular RBE No.
193/2019 dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 5 MP-3916-2025 11.11.2019,
whereby the scheme/policy providing appointment to land losers had already been withdrawn.

Therefore, the subsequent acquisition of educational qualification by the petitioner after the withdrawal of the policy could not have been taken into consideration for the purpose of appointment under the said scheme.
8. Apart from the aforesaid deficiency, the petitioner was also found to be ineligible on the ground of age.

As per Clause 5(x) of the notification dated 14.10.2016 issued by the West Central Railway Headquarters, the minimum age prescribed was 18 years and the maximum age limit was 32 years,
which was to be determined as on 01.01.2017.

As per the date of birth mentioned by the petitioner in his application form, his age on the cut-off date i.e. 01.01.2017 was 38 years and 4 months, which was clearly beyond the prescribed maximum age limit.
Thus, the petitioner was not eligible for appointments even on the ground of age.

9. The contention raised by learned counsel for the petitioner that he subsequently passed the 10th examination and therefore his claim ought to have been considered cannot be accepted in view of the settled legal position that the eligibility of a candidate has to be determined with reference to the cut-off date specified in the recruitment notification.
Since the petitioner did not possess the minimum educational qualification as well as the prescribed age eligibility on the relevant date, the authorities were justified in declining his claim.

10. The Central Administrative Tribunal, after considering the relevant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 6 MP-3916-2025 circulars issued by the Railway Board and the material placed on record
, has rightly come to the conclusion that the petitioner did not fulfill the essential eligibility criteria for appointment under the land acquisition scheme.
The Tribunal has therefore declined to grant any relief to the petitioner.

11. So far as reference made by the Tribunal to O.A. No.284/2025 in the impugned order is concerned, it is true that in the impugned order the learned Tribunal has made a reference to O.A.
No. 284/2025 while dealing with the petitioner's case.
However, even if the said reference is assumed to be inadvertent or not strictly applicable to the facts of the present case, the same does not affect the ultimate conclusion reached by the Tribunal.

The dismissal of the petitioner's Original Application is primarily founded on the undisputed fact that on the relevant cut-off date the petitioner did not possess the minimum educational qualification prescribed under the applicable policy and was also beyond the prescribed age limit.
These findings are based on the material available on record and the applicable circulars of the Railway Board.

Therefore, the mere reference to O.A. No. 284/2025 in the impugned order does not render the decision of the Tribunal illegal or Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97004155/
3 unsustainable.
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner had initially submitted his application under the policy dated 14.10.2016 seeking appointment on account of acquisition of his land.

However, as is evident from the record, at the time of submission of the application the petitioner did not possess the minimum NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 7 MP-3916-2025 educational qualification prescribed under the said policy.
The petitioner subsequently acquired the qualification of 10th standard only on 07.09.2021 and thereafter sought consideration of his claim.
By that time, the scheme/policy providing appointments to land losers had already been withdrawn by the Railway Board vide letter dated 11.11.2019.
Thus, the petitioner sought consideration of his claim at a stage when the policy itself was no longer in existence.

The contention of the petitioner that his application was rejected merely on the basis of a report submitted by the Land Acquisition Officer/Deputy Chief Engineer (Railway), who according to him was not the competent authority, also cannot be accepted.

From the material available on record it is apparent that the petitioner's application was submitted before the competent authority and the same has been rejected by the competent authority itself after due consideration of the relevant facts and applicable policy.
Therefore, the rejection of the petitioner's claim cannot be said to be vitiated on the ground alleged by the petitioner.

13. The contention of the petitioners that their applications were rejected merely on the basis of a report submitted by the Land Acquisition Officer/Deputy Chief Engineer (Railway), who according to them was not the competent authority, also does not merit acceptance.

From the material available on record, it is evident that the applications of the petitioners were duly placed before the competent authority and were rejected after due consideration of the relevant facts and the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 8 MP-3916-2025 applicable policy.

It is also significant to note that when the petitioners' first applications were rejected on the grounds of lack of the prescribed educational qualification, the said orders were not challenged by them at the relevant time.
Only after subsequently acquiring the qualification and facing rejection of their second applications have the petitioners sought to question the competence of the authority.
Such a contention, raised at a belated stage, cannot be permitted to be agitated and therefore deserves to be rejected.

14. In Misc. Petition No. 6992/2025 Manoj Kumar Mishra V/s Union of India, this Court has already taken the view that there is no dispute to the fact that, as of today, no policy for the grant of employment is available in the Railways.

entities.text: Misc. Petition No. 6992/2025 Manoj Kumar Mishra V/s Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The area of the acquired land was also very less to claim that livelihood has gone due to the acquisition of the land for the railway project.
Therefore, no writ can be issued to the respondents, and the petitioners are not entitled to relief.
15. It is the prerogative of the respondents to grant relaxation or not for the grant of compassionate appointment in addition to monetary compensation.
Consideringting the first application of the petitioner, the competent authority, after considering the claim, it means the competent authority decided not to give any relaxation to the applicant.
It is not permissible repeatedly that the applicant filed application for appointment after obtaining qualification.
Policy to give appointment is discretionary, not mandatory for every land loser.

Once respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 9 MP-3916-2025 denied the claim and petitioner did not challenge that Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97004155/
4 order; after passing more time to get qualification the applicant became over age.

entities.text: Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In every case applicant is not entitled to get relaxation in age or qualification, that provision applies for special case.
After 10 years passing it is not predictable to remand the case to competent authority.

16. In policy E(NG)II/2010/PC-5/1 dated 28/9/10 it is mentioned that applicant claiming appointment shall be required to submit the application with his/her signatures and photos duly certified by local MP, MLA or any Gazette Officer.
Candidates shall also submit affidavits fulfilling eligibility criteria stipulated in Para 2 above, duly certified by the Competent Authority/Land Acquisition Officer.
This shall be considered by respective Divisional Railway Managers.
The applicant should normally fulfill the eligibility and other conditions prescribed for the post against direct recruitment quota from open market.
In special cases, General Manager of the Railway can relax these conditions, and with respect of educational qualifications, applicant with capability shall also be considered.

17. In policy E (NG)II/2010/RC-5/1 dated 11/11/19 it is mentioned that the modalities for implementation of Serial No. 4 of the Second Schedule of the RFCTLARR Act 2013 were examined by Ministry of Railways and it has been decided that Ministry of Railways' earlier policy of offering appointment in Railways to affected land-losers issued vide references above is withdrawn and circulars issued in this regard NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 10 MP-3916-2025 vide reference above stand superseded.
18. Letter No. WCR/PHQ/Rect/122/Misc. Matter/Land Acquisition dated 5/3/21 stated that land looser who did not file application for appointment till 11/11/19, if they file application and fulfilled the qualification, that application will be considered, if land would be acquired before 11/11/19.

entities.text: Serial No. 4 of the Second Schedule
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
Chief Personnel Officer withdrew above letter dated 5/3/21 by letter No. WCR/PHQ/Rect/122/Misc.
Matter/Land Acquisition dated 07.03.2023.
19.

After considering the above all policy and circular it is very clear that after withdrawn the policy no repeated application be allowed, only those persons who cannot apply for appointment will submit his application.
After withdrawing the policy by letter dated 5/3/21 no new applicant files the application for appointment of job.
Application for appointments has already been rejected prior to getting qualifications hence applicant not entitled to get service in lieu of acquisition of land.

20. In exercise of powers of judicial review, this Court does not find any illegality, perversity or jurisdictional error in the impugned order dated 01.05.2025 passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal, Bench at Jabalpur.

entities.text: Central Administrative Tribunal, Bench at Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The findings recorded by the Tribunal are based on the applicable rules, circulars and the undisputed factual position regarding the petitioner's educational qualification and age on the relevant date.

21. Learned counsel reliance on the order of learned Tribunal in O.A. No. 745/2021 (Charan Prakash Kushwaha vs. Union of India) decided on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21372 11 MP-3916-2025 09.05.2022, in our view, that order is not binding on this Court.

entities.text: O.A. No. 745/2021 (Charan Prakash Kushwaha vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Tribunal,
while passing that judgment, misconceived the fact and provision of the policy, hence that judgment is not applicable to the present case.

The contention of learned counsel is also not applicable to the Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97004155/
5 present case that the action of the respondents is discriminatory, since in several similar cases the respondents have relaxed the educational qualification and granted appointment subject to the condition that the candidate would acquire the requisite qualification within a stipulated period.

entities.text: Rakesh Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The power to give appointments is a discretionary power according to the facts of the cases, hence it cannot be said that the action of the respondents is discriminatory.

22. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has failed to establish any legal right to claim appointment in the Indian Railways on the basis of land acquisition, particularly when he did not satisfy the prescribed eligibility conditions at the relevant time and the policy itself stood withdrawn subsequently.
22. Consequently, the present Miscellaneous Petition being devoid of merit is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
(VIVEK RUSIA) (PRADEEP MI  JUDGE JUDGE
